description: National Gap Analysis is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USGS, United States Geological Survey. Conservation scientists conduct a gap analysis to understand and protect biodiversity and threatened or endangered species. To assess if a species has adequate protection, they document the status, range, and distribution of plant communities and/or animal species’ habitats, and consider how much of the habitat is held by different conservation and resource management organizations. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
